product_scope: itpay is the single public CLI entry point, and $itpay is its user-facing Skill invocation. Under that one product entry point, the two top-level commerce actions are buy and sell: Buyer workflows are available now; Seller workflows use the same entry point via itpay sell.
title: Railway Query, Planning, and Ticket Booking
purpose: Choose the right railway service for the buyer's situation, submit the exact input contract each service expects, bridge a chosen train into booking via the server-issued selection, and follow the protected checkout flow without inventing field names.
when_to_use: The buyer wants train schedules, routes, or tickets.
A railway service execution fails at the geo, search, catalog, or recommend step.
The buyer only knows a city or fuzzy location rather than a station name.
The buyer asks about seat preferences, refunds, or ticket issuance status.
A query returned login_required or rate_limited.

service_selection.itpay-rail-exact: Use when the buyer knows BOTH the exact departure and arrival railway station names (e.g. 古镇 → 广州南). Direct train query, fastest path. Do NOT use it with only a city or fuzzy location.
service_selection.itpay-rail-smart: Use when the buyer has a city name, an area, an address, or wants transfer planning and recommendations. The platform resolves locations to stations itself; never silently convert a city into its namesake station.
service_selection.itpay-rail-booking: Purchase service — use ONLY after the buyer explicitly chose a train and seat from a query result. Starts quote → protected checkout → payment → asynchronous issuance on one execution. Never queried for schedules.
service_selection.svc_qizhidao_company_lookup: Not a railway service; do not mix intents.

required.origin: Departure railway station name only, e.g. 古镇. Not a city or an address.
required.destination: Arrival railway station name only, e.g. 广州南.
required.travel_date: Travel date in YYYY-MM-DD. The field name must be exactly travel_date; aliases like date are rejected.

itpay-rail-exact.optional: None. additionalProperties is false — extra fields are rejected by the provider.

required.origin: Fullest known departure location: city, district, area, or address is all acceptable.
required.destination: Fullest known arrival location, same rule as origin.
required.travel_date: Travel date in YYYY-MM-DD. The field name must be exactly travel_date.

optional.origin_city: Departure city hint that helps location resolution.
optional.depart_after: Do not depart before this time.
optional.arrive_before: Do not arrive after this time.
optional.priority: One of balanced | fastest | cheapest | safest | flexible.

preferred.passengers: Integer 1-5: number of passengers, NOT passenger identity records.

selection.token: The booking_offer.selection_token carried on the chosen result item.
selection.seat_type: Seat code when the user picked a specific class, e.g. O.

explicit_legs.legs: Array of 1-3 legs, each: from_station_code, to_station_code, travel_date, train_code, departure_time (HH:MM), arrival_time (HH:MM), arrival_days (int 0-7), seat_type. Only use when no booking_offer is available; never guess these values.

itpay-rail-booking.boundary: Identity fields (names, ID numbers, phones) never belong in this input; they are collected on the protected checkout page.

selection_flow: Exact results carry per-train candidates; smart results carry journeys. Bookable options carry booking_offer with a server-signed selection_token.

The token binds the stored result snapshot and the chosen option. Submit it with passengers (and seat_type when the user picked a class); the server derives the authoritative legs and re-quotes live. Do NOT hand-build legs JSON from the visible result.
An expired or foreign token returns a clear error; recover by running a fresh query or by explicit legs — never by guessing token contents.
Repeating the same selection restores the same booking execution instead of creating a second one.

trial_and_login.policy: itpay-rail-exact and itpay-rail-smart each allow 2 anonymous queries per enrolled device lineage — independent counters, not a shared pool of 4.
trial_and_login.login_required: Trial for that service is exhausted. The query is paused BEFORE provider calls; the execution keeps its input. Offer itpay auth login; after binding, resume the SAME execution with services run --execution <id> (no input file). Do not start a new execution, do not make the user re-describe the trip, and do not burn the other service's quota to dodge the gate.
trial_and_login.rate_limited: Registered accounts have no cumulative search cap but normal per-minute limits apply; wait retry_after_ms and resume the same execution.
trial_and_login.fourth_result: The 4th result is delivered first; only the next new query requires authorization.
trial_and_login.purchase_after_trial: Selecting a saved option and buying it does not consume search quota and works even when trial is exhausted.

flow: services start <service> --json returns input_required plus the guidance block for rail services.
Submit input with services run <service> --execution <id> --input-json <file> --json on the SAME execution.
itpay-rail-smart may stop at a location confirmation step; show the candidate places to the buyer, then continue the same execution after the human confirms.

After the buyer explicitly picks a train/seat, run itpay-rail-booking with the selection token (preferred) or explicit legs. The execution then pauses at the booking review (workflow:confirm_booking): services next returns booking_review_required with human_action.context.review carrying draft_revision, legs, seat_options and notice_version.

Collect the review input and submit it with services action <id> --action workflow:confirm_booking --actor-type human --status approved --input-json <file> --json. Required fields: draft_revision (exact server value), passengers, seat_type, seat_preferences (one entry per passenger_index 0..n-1, values limited to that leg's seat_options), party_preference, fallback=automatic_assignment, notice_version, accept_non_guaranteed=true. Only after an accepted review does the server quote and offer checkout.

The booking execution reaches a protected checkout: passenger identity data is entered by the human on that page, never through the CLI. Account authentication may happen inside checkout — do not force a separate auth login first (Path B).
Payment success does not mean the ticket is issued. Issuance is asynchronous; keep reading the same execution with services next.
If seat details are still syncing after issuance, advise the buyer to verify the itinerary on 12306 instead of repeating the query.

failure_handling.failed_step: The CLI reports failed_step and failed_step_meaning in the result when a workflow fails.
failure_handling.geo: Location resolution failed: check origin/destination are real place names, or attach origin_city/coordinate hints, then start a NEW execution (a failed execution is terminal).
failure_handling.search: Supplier query failed: most commonly a wrong field name (must be travel_date) or a nonexistent station name; recheck input against this doc.
failure_handling.catalog_or_recommend: Location resolved but no feasible trains: change the date or stations.
failure_handling.login_required_is_not_failure: login_required / rate_limited pause the execution; they are NOT failures and never justify a replacement execution.
failure_handling.general_rule: Never replay a failed execution and never guess different field names; correct the input and start a new execution of the same service.
failure_handling.booking_review_changed: The submitted draft_revision is stale: re-read services next for the current review projection and resubmit the full input; do not bump the revision yourself.

seat_preferences.meaning: A buyer's seat-letter preference may be planned per leg before payment. The plan is submitted to the supplier when encodable; unsupported combinations fall back to automatic assignment.
seat_preferences.letters: Evidence-backed letters only: O=ABCDF (second class), M=ACDF (first class), 9=ACF (business class). Other layouts auto-assign.
seat_preferences.boundary: Never claim a preference was fulfilled before supplier confirmation; check the issued seat in the order/status output.
seat_preferences.review_contract: Submitted inside the confirm_booking action via --input-json (nested JSON; --input key=value cannot express it and must not be combined with it). One preference per passenger slot, passenger_index 0-based. draft_revision must equal the server projection; a stale revision returns booking_review_changed — re-read services next and resubmit, never increment locally.
seat_preferences.revision: While payment has not started, the same execution accepts a revised review: resubmit confirm_booking with the new draft_revision; the old unpaid quote/checkout is retired and re-quoted. After a payment attempt the review is closed — never create a replacement purchase.

agent_rules: Pick the service by the buyer's input precision: exact station names → itpay-rail-exact; anything fuzzier → itpay-rail-smart; explicit purchase intent after a selection → itpay-rail-booking.
Never invent input field names. If the guidance block or this doc does not list a field, do not send it.
Never ask the buyer for passenger names, ID numbers, or phone numbers in chat; those are collected only on the protected checkout page.
Never reconstruct provider-shaped legs JSON when a booking_offer.selection_token is available; submit the token plus passengers.
Seat preferences are requests, not guarantees: always repeat the notice that automatic assignment remains possible, and never claim a specific seat before the issued order shows it.
Take draft_revision only from the current services next review projection; on booking_review_changed re-read instead of retrying the stale value.
login_required and rate_limited are pauses, not failures: resume the same execution, never spawn a replacement.
Do not repeat or replay a failed execution; correct the input and start a new one.
Do not claim payment equals ticket issuance; issuance is asynchronous and confirmed only by the issued seat status.

notifications.channels: Delivery notices reach the checkout-confirmed contact: email always works; a verified mainland SMS recipient is optional and checkout-scoped. The passenger phone, the login phone and the notification recipient are independent facts.
notifications.status_read: The order read exposes masked per-leg notification entries (keys: issued, details_pending, seat_ready) with channel, status and masked recipient — never raw numbers.
notifications.truthfulness: Provider acceptance is not delivery; an uncertain send outcome is reconciled, not silently retried. A notification failure never changes ticket or refund state; report it as a delivery detail, not an order failure.
notifications.unavailable: If SMS is not configured or a recipient is unverified, email still satisfies the contact policy — never present an unverified phone as enabled.
